result.summary: Do not ship: password changes no longer revoke stolen session cookies.

findings.title: Stolen sessions retain authenticated access after password changes
findings.body: Changing the password now preserves session_secret. An attacker holding a valid pre-change triggarr_session cookie can continue accessing protected routes after the owner changes their password: triggarr/web/middleware.py:144–148 validates only that cookie against the unchanged secret, and triggarr/auth.py permits it until its 30-day expiry. No replacement revocation check exists on this path. This removes the existing compromise-recovery protection and contradicts the session-eviction tests in tests/test_auth_routes.py:604–707.
findings.recommendation: Restore session-secret rotation alongside the password hash update and reissue the acting user's cookie under the new secret. Verify that another device's pre-change cookie is rejected after the change.

next_steps: Restore revocation and run the existing password-change session rotation, cookie reissue, and other-device eviction tests.
